Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 usage audit + proposed staged upgrade (prep for renewal)

Hi Elena / David —

Thanks again for taking time last week. Attached is the Q3 usage audit we promised (orchid_q3_usage_report.xlsx) plus a short latency trend chart (latency_trends_q3.png). High level notes:

- Total token consumption QoQ: +32% (growth driven by chat-heavy flows + embeddings reuse).
- Hot path latency increased ~85ms median for 512-token sequences in July; appears correlated with model mix shift to the larger variant.
- Prefix caching reduced repeat-forward costs by ~18% where implemented.

Given the consumption trajectory and your comment about tightening SLAs for customer-facing features, I sketched a staged upgrade approach to give predictable throughput while reducing per-token cost over the next 6 months. See the attachment for a one-pager.

Can you confirm if the team is open to: 1) moving from month-to-month to an annual committed tranche for 3x baseline, and 2) taking a short pilot of reserved capacity for the busiest routes? If yes I’ll loop in pricing and CS to put numbers to the plan.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm procurement window and any PO constraints
- Internal pricing + SLA ask (I’ll pull ops in)
- 30-min alignment call (can do Wed/Thu afternoon PT)

Thanks —
Avery

Thanks, Avery — this is helpful. Quick clarifications before we loop procurement:

1) Token mix: the increase you show — how much of that is embeddings vs. generative chat? Our billing allocation needs to map to feature teams.
2) Latency: the median bump you flagged — is that an intermittent regression (specific days) or an overall shift since July? We need to know whether to expect customer-facing regressions if we move more traffic to the larger model.

We are open to an annual commit if the economics are clear and there is a path to preserve our p95 latency for chat. We’d also like to explore a burst lane for spikes (peak hours). Procurement is on cc — they’ll want any amendment draft plus estimated monthly spend per tranche.

Can we do the alignment call on Thu 10/07 at 11:00am PT?

—Elena

Folks — forwarding Orchid.ai thread. They want clarity on token mix and latency behavior and are open to an annual commit + burst lane. Procurement is on cc and asked for an amendment draft and monthly spend per tranche.

Please see attached usage/latency artifacts. Key asks for pricing/legal:
- Three-tranche proposal: baseline (current commit), staged uplift (2.5x baseline), and peak tranche (3.5x with burst lane).
- SLA: maintain p95 latency <= 450ms for chat routes; propose a credit schedule if breached.
- Pilot: 30-day reserved pilot for busiest route before full tranche activation.

Ben — can you run numbers and propose the staged_pricing worksheet? Marissa — can you confirm CS ops capacity for pilot and call out any preflight work (prefetch, prefix caching enablement, telemetry hooks)?

I’ll own the customer coordination and calendar. Call scheduled Thu 10/07 11:00am PT (tentative).

Thanks,
Avery

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Q3 usage audit + proposed staged upgrade (prep for renewal)

Avery / Marissa — ran the numbers and attached a draft (staged_upgrade_pricing.xlsx). High level: 

- Baseline: keep current T&Cs at current effective rates; monthly average token spend baseline = $62k.
- Staged uplift (2.5x): committed monthly = $155k, effective per-token discount ~22% vs baseline; expect unit cost to drop as we route more to quantized smaller-variant for non-latency-critical flows.
- Peak tranche (3.5x + burst): committed monthly = $217k, includes 10% burst credit buffer for traffic spikes and an ops-runbook for burst activation.

ROI recap for Orchid (6 months): assuming 2.5x adoption of the uplifted routes and a 15% reduction in infra-induced errors (from improved model routing), Orchid nets estimated $78k in avoided costs and faster time-to-response for customers that convert better.

SLA ask — propose credit structure: 5% monthly credit if p95 > 500ms more than two consecutive weeks; 15% credit if p95 exceeds 700ms for a full month. Legal will need to draft an amendment — I suggest we prefill Redlines in amendment_draft.pdf and send to procurement after Thursday’s call.

Attachments: staged_upgrade_pricing.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB); amendment_draft.pdf (pdf, 45KB)

Ben
